summary: GRAVEYARD structural pass mapped every active-batch company across the AI/compute infrastructure chain. The cluster spans launch/space infrastructure, high-speed connectivity, compute accelerators, foundry/lithography, CPU IP, memory/networking and power/cooling. The strongest shared causal risk is not demand absence but common-mode hyperscaler capex, export/geopolitical constraints and bottleneck migration; explicit falsifiers remain open.

evidence: Space access + satellite systems connect launch cadence and national-security/communications infrastructure to downstream services
falsifiersUnknowns: reusable launch competition compresses economics; Neutron delay breaks scale path

evidence: AEC/optical connectivity is a bandwidth/power bottleneck relief layer between accelerators and scale-out fabrics; current revenue concentration confirms dependence on few AI builders
unresolvedGaps: successor optical architecture and customer insourcing
contradictions: Bottleneck importance is high but value capture can migrate into customer-designed silicon/optics
falsifiersUnknowns: co-packaged optics or in-house connectivity displaces merchant solution

evidence: PCIe/CXL connectivity addresses composability/memory-bandwidth constraints in heterogeneous compute
unresolvedGaps: end-customer mapping and durable CXL monetization
falsifiersUnknowns: CXL adoption stalls or integration moves into platform silicon

evidence: Accelerated compute sits at central AI training/inference bottleneck; concentration evidence shows causal dependence on a limited number of builders despite broad end demand
unresolvedGaps: inference commoditization and custom accelerator substitution rate
contradictions: Compute scarcity supports pricing, but hyperscaler custom silicon can migrate the bottleneck away from merchant GPU
falsifiersUnknowns: custom accelerators reach sufficient software/ecosystem parity; inference economics compress

evidence: Alternative accelerator/CPU supplier increases compute resilience and benefits if customers seek second-source capacity
Custom AI silicon + networking positions AVGO where hyperscalers migrate from general accelerators toward workload-specific compute
unresolvedGaps: customer concentration and custom-silicon bargaining power
contradictions: Custom silicon is both NVDA substitute and itself concentrated around few builders
falsifiersUnknowns: customers internalize design or networking value capture

evidence: Leading-edge foundry is a cross-vendor physical bottleneck supporting NVDA/AMD/AVGO/ARM ecosystems; exceptional Q2 margins indicate current scarcity/value capture
unresolvedGaps: geographic diversification economics and customer concentration
contradictions: Dominant bottleneck value is paired with Taiwan geopolitical single-region risk
falsifiersUnknowns: geopolitical interruption or viable leading-edge alternative closes process gap

evidence: EUV/High-NA lithography is upstream of leading-edge compute and memory; Q2 commitments imply customers are still expanding advanced capacity
unresolvedGaps: critical supplier single points and export-control demand migration
contradictions: Near-monopoly lithography bottleneck is powerful but politically exposed and dependent on specialized supplier network
falsifiersUnknowns: alternative patterning architecture becomes economically competitive; export restrictions structurally shrink served market

evidence: CPU architecture/IP links edge/mobile/cloud compute; concentrated Arm China/SoftBank relationships create governance/monetization chokepoints around otherwise broad technical adoption
unresolvedGaps: RISC-V substitution pace and related-party economics
contradictions: Architecture ubiquity does not equal diversified revenue capture
falsifiersUnknowns: RISC-V reaches ecosystem parity in key growth markets

evidence: HBM/memory bandwidth is a direct successor bottleneck as accelerator compute scales; memory cyclicality can turn scarcity into oversupply
unresolvedGaps: HBM supply-demand duration and capex response
contradictions: Structural HBM need coexists with commodity-cycle mean reversion
falsifiersUnknowns: capacity additions outrun AI memory demand

evidence: Ethernet scale-out networking connects accelerator clusters; rising cluster size increases fabric bandwidth/latency importance
unresolvedGaps: white-box/custom fabric substitution and large-customer dependence
contradictions: Open Ethernet expands TAM while also enabling alternative vendors/white-box architectures
falsifiersUnknowns: hyperscaler custom networking captures switching value

evidence: Power delivery and thermal management become physical successor bottlenecks after compute procurement; AI density raises cooling/power intensity
contradictions: Demand can remain structurally strong while project timing/backlog cancellation weakens realized economics
falsifiersUnknowns: AI capex slowdown or alternative cooling/power architectures commoditize incumbent value

contradictions: The active batch is heavily correlated to one causal super-cycle: AI/data-center capex. Cross-stack diversification does not equal demand-regime diversification.
Upstream bottlenecks can migrate: GPU scarcity -> HBM/networking -> power/cooling -> grid/energy; Earth should avoid treating today's chokepoint as permanent.
unknowns: Rate at which power/grid constraints cap compute deployment
peerRequests: Discovery lane: search for substitute architectures in optical interconnect, RISC-V, custom accelerators and cooling.
Red team: stress a synchronized hyperscaler capex slowdown across the entire 12-company cluster.
blockingIssues: Structural readiness remains incomplete until company-specific substitution probabilities and narrow queue blockers are evidenced.
